notes: EMULATED. No GitHub Actions run was made: the workflows have not been pushed. The duration is that of the committed fast.yml's own steps, run one after another in a Docker container made to resemble a GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runner (4 CPUs, the size GitHub lists for a public repository [V, GitHub documentation read 2026-10-24]; Ubuntu 24.04; git, curl, Python 3 and xz installed before the clock starts because the hosted image carries them). The clock runs from the first step's start to the last step's end.

What the emulation leaves out: queue time and runner start-up; GitHub's Actions cache, which setup-node would use for the npm cache (here every cache is cold, which is the slower case); the runner's tool cache, which holds Node (here it is downloaded and unpacked); GitHub's network; and the speed of a hosted runner's CPU. This host's cores are faster than a hosted runner's (not measured here), so a hosted run can take longer than these numbers; the headroom factor in values is the slowdown a hosted run could have before it exceeded the budget.

The container's 4 CPUs are a quota on this host's 20 logical CPUs, not 4 pinned cores, and the host was shared with other Docker jobs and agents while this was recorded; its load was not measured. The three runs and the 2-CPU run show how much the figure moved.

The checkout step copies this working tree (tracked files and untracked files that .gitignore lets through) and its .git, not a pushed commit: HEAD was 44d12a9395f1b60c44a37c8977bd529eeee35319 and the tree had uncommitted changes, which include the other W0 tasks' deliverables. The lane therefore ran over whatever those tasks had written at the time; a step that failed is listed in values.steps_failed (with the task that builds it: unit-tests: W0-S12; GATE-links: W0-T03; GATE-privacy: W0-T01), and its verdict line in the primary configuration says what it found. Those failures are those tasks' work in progress or an owner action, not a property of the lane; a red lane is recorded as it was. A step that fails early shortens the run (npm test, for one, skips the vendored-code tests once a workspace's tests fail), so a green lane would run a little longer than these runs; the difference is small against the headroom.

Overlay: the committed package-lock.json lacks a workspace package that a later task added (npm ci fails: Missing: @statespace/runs from lock file); the overlay is the lockfile that npm install --package-lock-only writes from the same manifests. The committed file hashes to 640f540a7770f99693575e0641a026652f49df8b7ac1f59b937fec3916afb57e and the overlay to 9f01a5036a191cc79546d4a6d69f4d30c5023a2b7902875ffb4779cda0a7e729; the difference is the new workspace's entries only. Until package-lock.json is regenerated (it is W0-S12's file), npm ci fails in the real fast lane: configuration fast-committed-lockfile is the same emulation on the committed file, and it stops at that step.

The 300 s budget is the lane runner's own (lane.mjs fast, counted from the first step, so the setup steps are inside it); the job's timeout of 6 minutes is only a backstop. In these runs the slowest step was "Run the fast lane" at 28.69 s.

The fast lane ran 13 steps and listed 15 gates as absent, because their scripts do not exist yet (each names the task that builds it); an absent gate is neither a pass nor a failure, and the lane gets slower as they arrive, which is what the budget watches.

The nightly configuration is the nightly lane run on this host with the host's Node and no container: it is not the digest-pinned Bench image (W0-T05's image is not published, so the BENCH_IMAGE variable cannot be set) and not GitHub. It shows that the lane writes status/nightly.json in the documented format; the generated file was moved under runs/ because status/nightly.json is a generated file that is never committed on the default branch (status/README.md).

actionlint 1.7.12 (archive checked against its published SHA-256) ran with shellcheck 0.11.0 from the shellcheck-py wheel; both exited without a finding on the four workflows. The same command on a scratch workflow with a planted shell fault and a planted misspelled expression found both (actionlint/planted.txt), so a clean exit means something. shellcheck came from a PyPI wheel run with `uv run --with`, which is not how a hosted runner would get it; it checks the scripts, not the runner.

Owner action that completes this record: push, require the check "fast lane" in the branch rules, dispatch fast.yml once (Actions > fast > Run workflow), read the run's duration from its page (first step start to last step end, as above) and add it as a configuration named github-hosted, then make it the primary configuration and set environment.emulated to false. The same run shows what the emulation missed.
